title: Platform Systems & Services: How‑Tos, Dashboards, Runbooks, Retrospective, and Roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview:
This document consolidates the platform engineering team’s canonical guidance for systems & services operations: core how‑tos, dashboard and alert configurations, runbooks for common incidents, a short retrospective from Q4 2025–Q1 2026, and the roadmap for Q2 2026. It is intended for oncall engineers, SREs, and platform and infra engineers that operate Redwood’s serving, orchestration, and observability stack.

Table of contents:
1) Summary and scope
2) Systems & services inventory (high level)
3) How‑tos (day‑to‑day operational tasks)
4) Dashboards and alerting (standard configs and thresholds)
5) Runbooks (incident playbooks)
6) Retrospective (Q4 2025–Q1 2026)
7) Roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities)
8) Ownership, escalation, and oncall rotations
9) References and links

1) Summary and scope
- Scope: All platform systems that support Redwood hosted and dedicated control plane features, primary observability and routing services, autoscaler controllers, and the GPU capacity manager.
- Excluded: customer private deployments (see eng-private-deployments/* for private runbooks).
- Goal: Provide a single reference that reduces time to mitigate P1/P2 incidents and standardizes dashboard/alert config and operational handoffs.

2) Systems & services inventory (high level)
- control-plane-api (service): REST API for account, model catalog, and routing policies. Owner: platform-svc team. SLO: p99 latency < 350ms, availability 99.95%.
- route-router (service): smart routing layer that selects model variant and region. Owner: routing team. SLO: p95 latency < 50ms for warm connections.
- autoscaler-controller (service): capacity autoscaling for Dedicated pools. Owner: capacity team. SLO: scale-up within 120s for urgent requests.
- cache-proxy (service): prefix/KV cache used for token reuse. Owner: caching team. SLO: hit rate > 60% for steady state.
- telemetry-pipeline (service): ingest/log/metric pipeline (Fluentd -> Kafka -> ClickHouse & Elastic). Owner: observability team. SLO: event delivery < 30s to analytics backends.
- gpu-fleet-manager (service): maintains node labels, health, and drain/orchestration. Owner: infra-gpu team. SLO: node reprovision cycle < 10 minutes for replacement.

3) How‑tos (day‑to‑day operational tasks)
A) Run a live query against production metrics (common checks)
1. Open the Platform Overview dashboard (Dash ID: platform-overview-prod).
2. Filter to service=control-plane-api and timeframe=Last 15 minutes.
3. Check p95/p99 latency, error rate (5xx) and request volume.
4. If errors > 0.5% and volume > 50 QPS, escalate to owner.

B) Restart a failing microservice (Kubernetes)
1. Confirm failures via logs: kubectl -n prod logs deploy/<service> --since=10m
2. If pod is OOMKilled or CrashLoopBackOff, inspect events: kubectl -n prod describe pod <pod>
3. If config change needed, create a patch in gitops: repo infra/overlays/prod/<service> and open PR with description and rollout plan.
4. To restart without config change: kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/<service> and monitor rollout status: kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/<service> --watch
5. Notify #platform-ops with PR link and incident context.

C) Scale Dedicated pool (manual override)
1. Use the Dedicated admin CLI: ./dedicated-admin scale --pool <pool-id> --desired <n> --reason "emergency-scale"
2. Confirm new capacity in gpu-fleet-manager UI and autoscaler-controller logs.
3. Postmortem: capture reason and metrics for 72-hour cost adjustment review.

4) Dashboards and alerting (standard configs and thresholds)
- Dashboard naming convention: team-service-environment-purpose (e.g., platform-control-plane-prod-overview).
- Core dashboards (must exist for every service): Overview, Errors, Latency, Resource Utilization, Deployment History.
- Alert categories and thresholds (baseline):
  - SEV P0 (P1) — Availability: Total 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 2 minutes OR service unavailable (no healthy backends). Pager: oncall + pagerduty. Example alert: control-plane-api_5xx_rate_high.
  - SEV P1 — Latency: p99 > 1s for 5 consecutive minutes for production request traffic > 10 QPS.
  - SEV P2 — Resource saturation: CPU or GPU memory > 85% for 5 minutes; Node unschedulable > 3 nodes.
  - SEV P3 — Degradation: Cache hit rate < 30% for 10 minutes.
- Alert routing rules:
  - route: SEV P0 -> platform-oncall -> escalation to engineering manager after 10m if ack not received.
  - SEV P1 -> platform-oncall -> SRE.
- Alert payloads must include: service, instance, recent error sample (up to 10 lines), time window, runbook link. Example: https://confluence.internal/platform-control-plane-runbook

5) Runbooks (incident playbooks)
- Each service must have a one-page runbook with: owner, oncall, critical paths, internal dependencies, debugger checks, mitigation steps, rollback steps, and postmortem trigger conditions.
- Canonical runbooks (quick reference):
  A) control-plane-api outage (P0)
  1) Verify incident in status page and Grafana (platform-overview-prod).
  2) Triage: determine whether failure is ingress, auth layer, database, or upstream routing.
  3) If database (pg-writer) is unhealthy: redirect reads to replica, switch writer if automated failover available, and notify DBA.
  4) If ingress LB healthy but pods unhealthy: scale replicas to 0 then back to desired to clear bad state, or roll back to last working image (gitops tag).
  5) If mitigation applied, update incident ticket and set mitigation expiry.
  6) Postmortem required if > 5 minutes downtime or customer impact > 5 accounts.

  B) autoscaler-controller failing to scale (P1)
  1) Check controller leader election: kubectl -n platform get endpoints autoscaler-controller-leaders
  2) Inspect controller logs for errors: kubectl -n platform logs deploy/autoscaler-controller --since=30m
  3) If controller is stuck reconciling requests, use manual scale as temporary measure (see section 3C).
  4) Create issue with logs, and tag capacity and infra-gpu teams.

  C) gpu node OOM / kernel panic (P1)
  1) Confirm via node exporter and node events.
  2) Cordon and drain node: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3) Create replacement via gpu-fleet-manager: /ops/gpu/reprovision --node <node-id> --reason "node-failed"
  4) Run a small smoke test by scheduling a synthetic inference job (service: runtime-smoke) and confirm success.

6) Retrospective (Q4 2025 – Q1 2026): key findings and action items
- Summary: The platform maintained 99.92% uptime across the hosted control plane. The primary incidents involved (a) autoscaler race condition during high-burst onboarding and (b) intermittent telemetry-pipeline lag during nightly bulk imports.
- Root causes:
  - Autoscaler: leader election and duplicate reconcile loops created transient over/underscaling under high short-lived request spikes.
  - Telemetry: backpressure on Kafka leads to retention/backlog growth during bulk import jobs; compaction and consumer lag rose.
- Actions taken:
  1) Autoscaler leader election fixed: added a lease duration guard and lowered reconcile frequency (PR #2213). Deployed 2026-01-12.
  2) Telemetry: raised Kafka partition throughput, added adaptive consumer parallelism, and added monitoring of consumer lag per-import-job.
  3) Added an emergency manual-scale playbook and runbook (see section 3C).
- Outstanding items (owners assigned):
  - Improve autoscaler unit tests and add chaos test (owner: capacity team, due 2026-03-15).
  - Implement priority tagging for bulk imports to avoid telemetry queue starvation (owner: observability, due 2026-04-01).

7) Roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities)
- Q2 OKRs for platform engineering (top priorities):
  1) Reduce average p99 latency for control-plane-api by 15% via kernel selection improvements + caching (owner: platform-svc, target: 2026-05-31).
  2) Improve autoscaler reliability: implement lease-based leader election and add metric alarms for leader churn (owner: capacity team, target: 2026-04-15).
  3) Observability: launch per-route cost and latency dashboards (owner: observability, target: 2026-06-01).
  4) Platform Howtos: publish standardized runbook templates and a self‑serve incident toolkit for engineers (owner: eng-platform, target: 2026-04-30).
  5) Oncall ergonomics: reduce noisy alerts by 40% via alert tuning and maintenance windows (owner: eng-sre, target: 2026-05-15).
- Roadmap milestones and rollout plan:
  - April: Complete autoscaler reliability changes and unit tests. Canary for leader election change in staging on April 8th, 2026; full rollout Apr 15th.
  - May: Deploy caching improvements and p99 latency measurement harness; collect 2 weeks of telemetry before final tuning.
  - June: Release per-route dashboards and cost telemetry; run a cross-team education session during week of June 10th.

8) Ownership, escalation, and oncall rotations
- Primary owners: platform-svc, capacity, observability, infra-gpu. Secondary owner: eng-platform operational team.
- Oncall rotation: 2-week rotation, primary oncall + secondary. Escalation: after 10 minutes unacknowledged P0 -> paging of manager oncall, 30 minutes unresolved -> exec notify.
- Contact matrix (Slack and PagerDuty):
  - platform-oncall (PagerDuty): rotation @platform-oncall
  - slack channel: #platform-ops (for async updates)
  - escalation manager: @eng-platform-manager

9) References and links
- Canonical runbooks: https://confluence.internal/eng-platform/runbooks
- Grafana dashboard list: https://grafana.internal/d/dash-list/platform-overview-prod
- GitOps repo for service overlays: git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-overlays.git
- Incident postmortem template: https://confluence.internal/templates/postmortem

Appendix: Runbook Template (one page)
- Title: <service> runbook
- Owner: <team>
- Oncall: <rotation>
- Key metrics: availability SLO, p95/p99 latency, error rate, resource saturation thresholds
- Quick checks: command snippets and dashboard names
- Mitigations: list of immediate mitigations (scale, rollback, restart, config flag toggles)
- Rollback steps: explicit gitops rollback commands and verification steps
- Postmortem trigger: > 5 minutes downtime OR > 3 customers impacted OR billing impact > $5k

If you are an oncall engineer: follow the runbook above, keep the incident timeline updated, and escalate per the contact matrix. After resolution, create a retro ticket and link it to the platform retrospective board.

Document maintenance: This document is maintained by the eng-platform team. For edits: open a PR against confluence-content (repo: docs/confluence-snapshots) and add reviewers: @platform-leads and @eng-sre.
